Inglewood, California
  April 9, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, April 9, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
Mayor Butts called the City Council into session for Closed Session at the hour of
1:02 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Padilla, and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  Council Members Dotson, and Morales.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:03 p.m. for Closed Session
Item Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, Finance Authority, and Parking Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority
Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as
follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance
  Authority Members Padilla, Morales and Franklin;
  and
  Absent:  Council  Member/Successor  Agency
  Member/Housing Authority Member/Finance
  Authority Member Dotson.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority
officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer* (Arrived at 2:03 p.m.)
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  1
 April 9, 2019

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Finance
  Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
  Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  Chris Mackenty spoke concerning Agenda Item No. DR-1, Staff report to provide
  a written update on the direction given by the City Council regarding the adoption
  of Ordinance No. 19-07 (45-Day Moratorium Limiting Rent Increases on Certain
  Residential Properties).

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Padilla that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, April 4, 2019, in the amount of $1,592,457.57,
  are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing
  Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said
  demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member Dotson.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  denial of the following claims:

  a) Edwin Baires for property damage on December 25, 2018.
  b) Cathy McKinney for personal injury on February 12, 2019.
  c) Tanisha Turner for property damage on December 13, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla and carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  101&301  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-058 APPROVED – REMY
  MOOSE MALEY, LLP; RESOLUTION NO. 19-038 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 BUDGET. Staff report dated April 9,
  2019, was presented recommending approval of an Amendment to Agreement
  No. 18-058 with Remy Moose Maley, LLP for legal services associated with the
  Environmental Review of a National Basketball Association Arena and associated
  facilities near the intersection of Prairie Avenue and Century Boulevard.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Approve Amendment to Agreement
  No. 18-058 in the amount of $225,000 (total contract amount of $550,000); and 2)
  Adopt Resolution No. 19-38 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2018-2019 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  PROVIDE FUNDING FOR CERTAIN PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  FOR ASSOCIATED FACILITIES NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF
  PRAIRIE AVENUE AND CENTURY BOULEVARD

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  2
 April 9, 2019

  142  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-018 APPROVED – SOUTH
  BAY CITIES COUNCIL; AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE 6 EXTENDING
  THE TERM TO FEBRUARY 28, 2021 AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated
  April 9, 2019, was presented recommending approval of the First Amendment to
  Agreement No. 19-018 with the South Bay Cities Council of Governments to
  allow the City to advance payment to SBCCOG for allowable project costs of the
  South Bay Slow Feasibility Study, prior to reimbursement from Caltrans.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Approve First Amendment to
  Agreement No. 19-018; and 2) Authorize amendment to Article 6 (Terms of
  Agreement No. 19-018), extending the term to February 28, 2021, to align with
  the Restricted Grant Agreement between the City and Caltrans.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 142  RESOLUTION NO. 19-39 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2018-2019 ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated April 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2018-2019
  Annual Budget and authorized position classification count.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Authorize adjustments to the Fiscal
  Year 2018-2019, Annual Budget as specified; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 19-39
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2018-2019 ANNUAL
  BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 173  AMENDMENT TO THE INGLEWOOD EXECUTIVE ORGANIZATION
  (IEO) MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – ACKNOWLEDGED
  AND AFFIRMED. Staff report dated April 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending City Council acknowledgement and affirmation of the
  modification implemented by the City Manager (per Article Eight, Section VI –
  Amendments to Memorandum of Understanding) to amend the Inglewood
  Executive Organization (IEO) Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) (Adopted
  December 6, 2016 (effective from October 1, 2016 – December 31, 2020)) related
  to Article Two, Section XI (Post Certificate Incentive Pay – Police Chief and
  Article Three, Section II-Supplemental Executive Compensation).

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby acknowledge and affirm to amend the
  Inglewood Executive Organization (IEO) Memorandum of Understanding. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  3
 April 9, 2019

 178  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT NO. SSP141811 APPROVED –
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AGING
  AND COMMUNITY SERVICES AND CITY OF INGLEWOOD. Staff
  report dated April 9, 2019, was presented recommending approval of Amendment
  No. 3 to Agreement No. SSP141811 between County of Los Angeles Workforce
  Development, Aging and Community Services and City of Inglewood, related to
  the provision of Care Management Services for Senior Citizens and Disabled
  Adults.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 3 to
  Agreement No. SSP141811. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.
 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-168 APPROVED – BETTER 4 YOU MEALS;
  SIGNING OF DOCUMENTS – APPROVED; PAYMENT OF
  OUTSTANDING INVOICES APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 19-40
  ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 BUDGET. Staff
  report dated April 9, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an
  agreement with Better 4 You Meals for the provision of breakfast, lunches, and
  snacks for the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food
  Service Program (SFSP) from March 1, 2019, through August 31, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-168 with
  Better 4 You Meals; 2) Approve the signing of documents associated with the
  California Department of Education (CDE) Summer Food Service Program and
  Child and Adult Care Food Program; 3) Approve payment of outstanding invoices
  in an amount not to exceed $104,638.50; and 4) Adopt Resolution No. 19-40
  entitled:

  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD APPROVING
  CERTAIN DOCUMENTS WITH THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION FOR THE CITY TO
  CONDUCT THE SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM AND
  CHILD AND ADULT CARE FOOD PROGRAM AND
  GRANTING THE MAYOR THE AUTHORITY TO SIGN ALL
  CONTRACT AMENDMENTS AND RELATED DOCUMENTS
  OF SAID PROGRAMS WITHOUT THE NEED OF FIRST
  BRINGING SAID ITEMS TO THE CITY COUNCIL

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 178  RESOLUTION NO. 19-041 ADOPTED – RE-APPROVING THE USE OF
  ASSET FORFEITURE FUNDS AND AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2018-2019 BUDGET. Staff report dated April 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution re-approving the use of $282,192 in Asset
  Forfeiture funds for the purchase of a modular office building from Aries
  Building Systems (Agreement No. 18-216).

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Re-approve use of Asset Forfeiture
  Funds; 2) Authorize the use of $160,000 for new expenditures; and 3) Adopt
  Resolution No. 19-041 entitled:

  4
 April 9, 2019

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE USE OF $443,192 IN ASSET
  FORFEITURE FUNDS FOR POLICE DEPARTMENT EXPENDITURES AND
  AMENDING THE 2018-2019 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

 178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – MERIDIAN RENTAL GROUP. Staff report
  dated April 9, 2019, was presented recommending authorization to pay an
  outstanding invoice from Meridian Rental Group for the rental of 32 barriers used
  for crowd safety and traffic control.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $8,797. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts and;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.

 183  AWARD OF CONTRACT AND APPROVE AGREEMENT NO. 19-169 –
  CLICKSOUND & STAGE. Staff report dated April 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending award of contract and approval of a three-year agreement with
  Clicksound & Stage for production services, backline and audio rentals for the
  City of Inglewood Earth Day Music Festival and Environmental Awareness
  event, as per Request for Bids No. 0110.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby award contact and approve Agreement
  No. 19-169 in the annual amount of $42,425.57 (includes a 15% contingency in
  the amount of $5,333.77). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts and;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.

 131.8  PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING INVOICES FOR HOLIDAY MOTEL
  AND PARKVIEW MOTEL – APPROVED. Staff report dated April 9, 2019,
  was presented recommending authorization to pay outstanding invoices submitted
  by two motels for emergency shelter services in the total amount of $24,960.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby 1) Approve payment to Holiday Motel
  in the amount of $6,480; and 2) Approve payment to Parkview Motel in the
  amount of $18,480. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts and;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.

 131.8  WRITTEN UPDATE ON THE DIRECTION GIVEN BY THE CITY
  COUNCIL REGARDING THE ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 19-07.
  Staff report dated April 9, 2019, to provide a written update on the direction given
  by the City Council regarding the adoption of Ordinance No. 19-07 (45-Day
  Moratorium Limiting Rent Increases on Certain Residential Properties).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Mayor Butts that the
  City Council extends the Moratorium for an additional 60 days. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts and;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.

  5
 April 9, 2019

 219  CITY TREASURER – MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report
  dated April 9, 2019, was presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for
  the Month ending December 31, 2018.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown,
  congratulated the City on their First-Time Homebuyers Program. She reminded
  everyone that the Treasurer’s Community Workshop will be held at City Hall on
  April 27, 2019, in Community Room A from 10:00 a.m. until 1:30 p.m. She
  stated at this workshop residents will learn about Reverse Mortgages, renters
  insurance, and the importance of burial cost. Lastly she stated an attorney will be
  present to discuss Wills and Trust.

 180  CITY OF INGLEWOOD FIRST-TIME HOMEBUYER PROGRAM.
  Harjinder Singh, Deputy to the City Manager, gave a brief report on the City of
  Inglewood’s First-Time Homebuyer Program. He encouraged those that are
  interested in purchasing their first home to come out on Monday, April 22, 2019,
  at 6:00 p.m. in the City of Inglewood City Hall, Community Room A.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Tiffany Wallace spoke concerning the importance of rent control.

  Chris Mackenty asked the City Council to consider back dating the rent control
  moratorium.

  Morris Griffin, Big Money Griff, spoke concerning the rent control issue.

  Erick Holly invited everyone to attend the State of the City address on April 18,
  2019, at the Hyatt LAX. He stated that rent control is a huge problem as a whole.

  Speaker Unknown, commented she has been displaced from her home due to new
  owners of the building.

  Ray Davis, 2nd District, commented he hopes closure is found with the
  displacement of residents. He also commented he feels that “Nipsey Hussel” was
  trying to do well for his community.

  Willie Agee commented he feels that everyone wants to move in the City of
  Inglewood due to the coming attractions.

  Sa’zar Price, thanked the City Council for extending the moratorium.

  Jim Vaughn, 2nd District, commented he is saddened to hear about the loss of a
  Highway Patrol Officer, a Police Officer, and Nipsey Hussel. He also encouraged
  those that are going through difficult times, to speak to a mental health doctor.

  Brice, (No last name given), stated help is needed for residents who are being
  displaced.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at 2:49 p.m.

  Approved this 30th day of April, 2019

  6
 April 9, 2019

  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk
